steps.title: A ت, tucked inside the root
body: Form VIII's signature is a ت infixed right after the first root letter, giving the shape اِفْتَعَلَ.
اِشْتَرَى ("to buy"), already in your vocabulary since A1, is a Form VIII verb — root ش-ر-ي: اِشْتَرَتِ الطَّالِبَةُ كِتَابًا, "the student bought a book," present tense تَشْتَرِي.

Form VIII often carries a reflexive or middle-voice sense — doing something for yourself. Patterns aren't fixed rules, though: اِشْتَرَى doesn't transparently mean "to seek to sell" from ش-ر-ي's buy/sell sense — it's simply lexicalized as "to buy."

steps.title: Form VIII in one sentence
steps.intro: Read the sentence, then check what marks it as Form VIII. Tap 🔊 to hear it.

steps.title: Spot the pattern
steps.prompt: اِشْتَرَى has a ت right after the first root letter (ش). Which form is that?
steps.explanation: اِفْتَعَلَ infixes ت after the first root letter — Form VII instead prefixes اِنْ with no ت, and Form X prefixes the longer اِسْتَ.

steps.title: Meaning tendency
steps.prompt: What tendency does Form VIII often carry?

options.label: A reflexive or middle-voice sense — doing something for yourself
No fixed meaning ever applies — every Form VIII verb is pure coincidence
A reciprocal sense, the same as Form III

steps.explanation: Form VIII's infixed ت often adds a middle-voice sense. That's a tendency, not an iron rule — اِشْتَرَى itself has drifted to simply mean "to buy" — but it's the pattern's usual direction.

steps.title: Seven forms down
steps.message: Form VIII — ت infixed, often reflexive/middle-voice. One form left: Form X.
